label: Two adapter tests assert the core through an alias instead of the adapter: codex/stop-arm.mjs:143 exports findCodexPid and hermes/session-end-arm.mjs:140 exports findHermesPid, both re-exports of findLoopChildPid, and codex-adapters.test.cjs:504 / hermes-adapters.test.cjs:292 call those aliases with the same table and the same 41-to-60 expectation relaunch-core.test.cjs:919 already asserts. Deleting the target resolution from either arm path leaves every test green. Fix: drive the Hermes armPendingRecord with its existing processTable/spawn seam, and hoist Codex's call into an identical exported armPendingRecord(dependencies) before asserting the spawned --target-pid.

The conformance table has no arm case, so the decision it exists to protect is outside it: the file states its purpose at adapter-conformance.test.cjs:6 but the table carries only three seed cases (:233) and four nudge cases (:258), all instruction text, and never arms a record, so kill-target resolution, the note-state rule and the live-killer suppression have no shared row. Fix: add an ARM_CASES table over a prepared pending record with an injected process table, reusing the existing in-process preparePending call at :279 and the child-process drivers.

tests/README.md pins an exact five-line test summary (tests 510, pass 510, fail 0 at README.md:98) while the same file tells a contributor to add a test for new adapter behavior (README.md:82), so following the document invalidates its own expected result. Fix: state the invariant (fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 0) and describe the total as growing with added cases, keeping 510 in the phase record that measured it.

direction: Proving the README's 510 total by counting test() calls statically
reason: Loop-generated conformance cases and node's subtest accounting make a static count unreliable, so the finding rests on the number being a snapshot rather than on it being wrong
